title: The economics of the takeaway
text: The delivery app has changed the restaurant industry more quickly than anyone {{1}} have predicted a decade ago. Dishes that once {{2}} a full restaurant evening can now be sold from a tiny kitchen with no dining {{3}} at all. For customers, the gains are obvious: choice, speed, and the pleasure of restaurant food {{4}} home. The economics are less comfortable. Apps commonly retain up to thirty per cent of each order, which many independent kitchens describe as the {{5}} between profit and loss. Some have responded by publishing 'direct order' prices, quietly {{6}} customers to bypass the apps. Cities, meanwhile, are rewriting zoning rules as delivery-only kitchens multiply in unexpected {{7}}. What nobody doubts is that the change is permanent: convenience, once tasted, is rarely {{8}} up.

gaps.explanation: 'anyone would have predicted' — hypothetical past prediction.
'required a full restaurant evening' — formal necessity.
'quietly encouraging customers to bypass' — encouraging + object + to-infinitive.
